newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican international reserves, assets rise.
newsitem.headline: Mexican international reserves, assets rise.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said on Tuesday its net international assets as of Nov. 29 were $5.023 billion, compared with $4.725 billion on Nov. 22.
The central bank said that its net international reserves rose to $16.317 billion from $16.257 over the same period.
It said the increase of $298 million in international assets in the week was due to:
- Net revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) of $219 million
- Net purchases of foreign currency from the federal government worth $14 million.
- Purchases of $123 million from banks, because of dollar put options exercised that had been placed on the market on Oct. 31.

- A net loss of $58 million for a combination of factors including changes in the dollar value of non-dollar assets and liabilities held by the bank; net returns on interest rates and from trading of metals and securities; and net deposits in dollar accounts of commercial banks at the central bank.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
